newsitem.title: UK: Allianz says UK purchase possible in future.
newsitem.headline: Allianz says UK purchase possible in future.

text.p: German insurer Allianz AG Holding said on Wednesday it had no immediate plans for acquisitions in Britain or France but refused to rule out purchases in the future.

The comments came as the company which owns Britain's Cornhill Insurance prepared to hold its first board meeting in London -- a tribute to London's status as a leading financial centre, said Allianz chief executive Dr Henning Schulte-Noelle.
While here, it plans to hold a series of meetings with investors and analysts.
Schulte-Noelle said Allianz had been "very happy" with the performance of Cornhill since it was bought in 1986.
But in the medium or long term, it may be advisable "to look for more size" through acquistions as well as internal growth, he said.
The same was true of its position in the French market, he added. "We're not one of the leading players in the market and in the medium or long term an acquisition is possible."
French state insurance Group GAN is one possibility, if its privatisation goes ahead under the new French socialist government.
"We readily admit that if GAN were privatised it would be of interest to us," said Schulte-Noelle.

Allianz, which operates in around 55 countries world-wide, has no plans to pursue acquisitions to regain its number one position in Europe now ceded to AXA-UAP following the merger of French insurance groups AXA and UAP announced last November.
Schulte-Noelle repeated company forecasts of moderate but double digit growth in profits for 1997 and around 11 percent growth in premium income.
